responses.response: Use the deployment kinds from the shared spec: `Node_Environment`, `Zone`, `Node_Vm`, and `Node_App`. The base shape for production should be `Environment -> Zone -> VM -> Node_App`. For your platform, a clean structure is: `Prod = Node_Environment`, then zones such as `Dmz`, `AppTier`, `ProcTier`, and `DataTier`, then VMs like `ProdApigwVm`, `ProdUploadVm`, `ProdWorkerVm`, and `ProdMongoVm`, and inside each VM a `Node_App` that represents the deployed runtime. Link each runtime to the logical model with `instanceOf`, for example `apiGwApp instanceOf documentPlatform.apiGateway`, `uploadApp instanceOf documentPlatform.uploadService`, `workerApp instanceOf documentPlatform.processingWorker`, and `mongoApp instanceOf documentPlatform.mongoDb`. Add rich Markdown descriptions to every zone and VM: zone descriptions should capture VLAN/CIDR, gateway, firewall, and purpose; VM descriptions should start with `eth0` and then list OS, CPU, RAM, Disk, Port, Monitoring, and RTO. Do not manually copy normal application relationships in deployment. Once a `Node_App` uses `instanceOf`, LikeC4 inherits the logical relationships automatically. Only add deployment-specific edges for infrastructure concerns such as monitoring, backups, bastion access, replication, or explicit operational network hops.

This skill is the right one for the base deployment framework: it tells you to model `Node_Environment -> Zone -> Node_Vm -> Node_App`, use consistent VM naming, add rich infrastructure descriptions, and connect runtimes with `instanceOf`. If your main goal is specifically how to split production into `Dmz`, `AppTier`, `ProcTier`, and `DataTier` and define firewall rules between those zones, switch to `structure-deployment-tiers`. Keep the boundary explicit: this skill covers honest infrastructure modeling; `structure-deployment-tiers` is the next step for tier organization and firewall design.

If production runs on managed Kubernetes and you do not know the underlying hosts, do not invent hidden physical VMs just to force the diagram into a VM-shaped model. Keep an explicit deployment hierarchy at the level you actually know. In this repository, `Node_Cluster` exists in the shared deployment spec, so an honest structure is `Prod = Node_Environment -> AppTier = Zone -> ProdK8s = Node_Cluster -> apiApp/uploadApp/workerApp = Node_App`. Then wire each runtime node back to the logical model with `instanceOf`, for example `apiApp instanceOf documentPlatform.apiGateway`, `uploadApp instanceOf documentPlatform.uploadService`, and `workerApp instanceOf documentPlatform.processingWorker`. Put known platform facts on the zone or cluster description instead of fabricating VM details. Normal application traffic is still inherited through `instanceOf`; only add deployment edges for true infrastructure-only interactions. If the discussion shifts into DMZ/AppTier/ProcTier zoning or firewall boundaries, route that part to `structure-deployment-tiers`.

Those deployment relationships should generally not be added for normal application traffic. The `HTTPS`, `HTTP/8080`, database port, or similar technology details belong on the system-model relationships, not duplicated in `deployment.c4`. For example, put the protocol on the logical edges such as `web -> api { technology 'HTTPS' }` and `api -> db { technology 'TCP/27017' }` or whatever logical relationship kind your model uses. In deployment, make the runtime nodes `Node_App` instances and link them with `instanceOf`; the deployed instances inherit those logical relationships automatically. Reserve explicit deployment relationships only for infrastructure-specific exceptions such as Prometheus scraping, replication, backup agents, log shipping, bastion access, or an operational network hop that is not represented in the logical model.

Add the Prometheus-to-API scrape as a deployment relationship, because that is an infrastructure-specific runtime concern. For example, model Prometheus as its own deployment node and add a scrape edge to the API runtime instance. Keep the API runtime tied back to the logical model with `instanceOf`, so its normal application relationships are inherited. Do not duplicate browser -> API traffic or API -> database traffic in deployment just to visualize them again; those belong in the logical model and flow through automatically to deployed instances via `instanceOf`. In short: add the monitoring scrape in deployment, avoid redrawing normal user/service/data traffic there, and only add other deployment edges when they are true operational exceptions such as backup, bastion access, replication, or log collection.
